Fundraising is intimidating. I designed a place where it isn’t.

RoleProduct Design (UI/UX) Intern
TimelineJul 2026 to Aug 2026
ToolFigma
Scope100+ mobile screens, design system
01

The problem

Founders and investors are trying to find each other.

Right now that happens across five tools. Cold email to reach out. Calendly to book. Zoom to meet. Notion to share the deck. A spreadsheet to track the cap table.

Nothing connects. Nobody tells you the rules.

Catalyst puts connecting, navigating and booking in one place.

02

Why it feels intimidating

Three things, visible in every step of a raise:

You don’t know why you were picked, or passed on.

You don’t know what happens after you send.

You don’t know the rules, and asking feels like admitting you don’t belong.

The design attacks all three.

03

Every match explains itself

A fit score alone is just another opaque judgment.

So each match carries its reason in plain language: their thesis names your sector, your stage, and your city.

The investor’s thesis appears in their own words. Checks, stage, portfolio count, whether they lead.

You read what they want before you decide to reach out.

04

Reaching out has a number on it

2 of 3 intro requests left today.

A limit answers the question a first time founder can’t answer alone: am I allowed to contact this person?

Yes. That’s what they’re for.

05

Matches arrive on a rhythm, not a feed

Six new founders, curated Monday morning. Next batch in three days.

Anything you haven’t opened carries over.

A raise takes months. A feed makes it feel like an emergency.

06

Booking happens where the match happens

You accept, then you pick the length. 15, 30 or 45 minutes.

Times already on your calendar show greyed out, not hidden. You can see the constraint.

They pick one. It lands on both calendars automatically.

No Calendly link. No back and forth email.

07

The confirmation screen states the rules

Most products confirm and stop. This one tells you what happens next:

A reminder goes to both sides 24 hours before.

Either side can reschedule once, without spending an intro request.

After the call, you both confirm it happened. No shows return the intro to your balance.

That last line matters most. You are not punished for someone else flaking.

08

One calendar for intros and events

Catalyst events in gold. Personal intros in green.

Export sends a live feed, so reschedules update in Google or Outlook without re importing.

09

Events lower the stakes of a first contact

Not everyone is ready to ask a stranger for money.

Listings tell you what you’re walking into: 21 investors attending, 8 write pre-seed checks. 3 pitch slots left. 14 climate investors.

10

The product teaches its own rules

SAFEs & Cap Tables 101. Template walkthrough included. 112 going.

Diligence Clinic: Reading a Cap Table.

The most intimidating part of a process is not knowing its rules. So the product teaches them.

11

Onboarding tells you why, not just what

Each profile field is labelled with its reason.

Accreditation status: required by law.

Stage and industries: investors filter by these.

Profile photo: recommended.

You know what’s mandatory and what isn’t. You go live at your own pace.

12

It admits what it can’t do

The cap table tool opens with a warning: manual tracking only, all SAFE agreements must be executed off platform.

A product that let a first time founder assume they were legally covered would be doing the exact thing this one exists to stop.

13

Scope

Onboarding, matching, messaging with company context in the header, intro scheduling, calendar, events, saved lists, deal pipeline, cap table modelling.

Both sides of the marketplace, fully designed.

100+ mobile screens in Figma, assembled from one system and specified for the developers building the app.

14

Outcome

Explored three design directions and presented them to the founding team. One was selected and taken into production.

Built the design system: typography, colour, surfaces, avatars, buttons, spacing and navigation.

Designed 100+ mobile screens in Figma and specified them for the developers building the app.

It still needs to be tested in the real market.
